subject: Decision Making
title: The Classic Trolley Problem
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Classic Trolley Problem.

hook.text: A trolley is heading toward five people. You can pull a lever to divert it to a track with one person. Do you pull?

buildup.text: Most people say yes: save five, sacrifice one. The math is simple. The morality seems clear.

discovery.text: But you actively caused that one death. Without your intervention, you are blameless. Action makes you a killer.

twist.text: The Classic Trolley Problem shows that the best decision is often not the most intuitive one.

climax.text: The Classic Trolley Problem matters because structure beats guesswork when stakes are high.

punchline.text: Pull the lever, save five, kill one. Simple math, impossible morality.

quiz.question: What moral conflict does the trolley problem expose?
options: The tension between maximizing lives and the rule against directly causing a death
